compatNote: COMPATIBILITY FLOOR the base states and every addition inherits (v5 version spine, V5-PLAN 2.2). Floors plus a single proven point, never a support matrix: rolling latest-only means the gate proves exactly one (dw, apps, swift tag) triple per run, and what it proved is recorded upward in layers/INDEX.json gateProven - written by the Foundry, never by hand. `dw.min` is the platform floor, `dw.tfm` the single target framework the host must build against, `swift.tag` the dynamicweb/Swift release tag (the 3-digit `swiftVersion` above is the same release without the tag form). `apps[].required: false` is an optional companion app: absent is fine, present below `min` is not. An addition MAY restate `compat` in its own layer.json to raise a floor; it may never lower one.
minSerializerVersionDeprecated: DEPRECATED ALIAS, not a second floor. The one serializer floor is compat.apps[id=Truvio.Commerce.Serializer].min: the Foundry compat leg (Test-CompatFloors) and the dw-demo-base install step read that key and nothing else. This field repeats the same value for prose readers that still name it (dynamicweb/skills dw-users-permissions page-gating.md); tools/ci/Validate-Distribution.ps1 fails when it disagrees with compat.apps, so it can never state a different number. Raise compat.apps and this field together; remove this field once no reader names it.
serializerTaughtSurfaceNote: WHY THE FLOOR IS 1.0.2-beta (base 3.4.2). Layers ship serialized SqlTable rows: sample-data 4.0.0 ships its whole demo dataset as merge-mode SqlTable YAML with a per-document ownership header, and feature-rma ships its RMA rows the same way. Three engine facts set the floor. (1) SqlTable NULL round trip: Truvio.Commerce.Serializer 1.0.1-beta and earlier wrote a NULL column as 1900-01-01 / '' / 0 in Merge mode on a row where an empty-string column came before the NULL (Serializer issue #18); 1.0.2-beta is the first release that writes it back as NULL, so an older engine silently corrupts shipped rows. (2) PackageUnzip, the transport an online build uses to move a layer's files, is available from 1.0.1-beta. (3) The ownership header needs 1.0.0-beta or later: a 0.9.x engine fails strict on the unknown ownership column. The engine's taught surface (the skills corpus and the Foundry harness) may run ahead of this floor; the floor rises only when a layer ships something an older engine drops, rejects or corrupts. Raise compat.apps[id=Truvio.Commerce.Serializer].min and minSerializerVersion together, not this note.
description: Machine-readable guarantees the base layer makes to every addition (v3.0 Distribution, base 3.0.0 FRAMEWORK-ONLY). The Swift 2.4 base split moved ALL content (both mode trees) and UrlPath to the surface-swift layer; the base now ships only the framework SQL sets + this contract + SQL-predicate config. Additions (feature/sample-data/surface/theme layers) bind ONLY to this contract - never to each other. Content-scoped contract bits (content areas, langPrefix, navDepth, page anchors, title rules, per-environment Area exclusions, protected Swift item types) moved to layers/surface-swift/surface.contract-notes.json. The gate reads this file for the base-contract collision check.

idRules.nvarcharPkNote: When an addition writes rows into a base-owned table whose PK is nvarchar (most Ecom tables - PriceId, PaymentId, ProductId, etc.), it MUST namespace the PK with a PACK-<NAME>- prefix (uppercase layer name). Keeps additions disjoint from the base and from each other.
idRules.intIdentityNote: When an addition writes SqlTable rows keyed by an int-identity PK, it MUST reserve an id at or above the 100000 floor. The floor does not reach _content item-instance ids (ItemType_<systemName> rows written through a page or paragraph): ItemType_* Id is a non-identity nvarchar the platform allocates on insert, and the Serializer content provider re-creates item rows by page/paragraph uniqueId, so the target assigns its own id and a YAML fields.Id never lands as the stored id. fields.Id in _content is informational only; no validator checks an item-id floor on _content. The floor applies to the int ids a layer MINTS. The AccessUser ids this contract names in guaranteedRows.permissionGroups are the one explicit exception: the permission groups 1325 / 1270 / 1292 are base-owned and sit below the floor by contract, and the base ships exactly those ids as SqlTable rows. Every identity the sample-data layer mints is above the floor (the B2B account 100100 and the personas 100101 / 100102 / 100103). Any other id below 100000 is out of contract. No validator checks the int-identity floor; it is an authoring rule.
idRules.baseCatalogNote: The base ships ZERO catalog (scaffolding-only, swift/2.3.2): EcomGroups, EcomProducts, EcomGroupProductRelation, EcomVariantGroups, EcomVariantsOptions, EcomVariantOptionsProductRelation, EcomDiscount, EcomDiscountTranslation, EcomPrices carry no base rows. The collision surface for these tables is addition-vs-sample-data-vs-addition, arbitrated statically by the gate.
idRules.reservedFixtureNote: The sample-data layer's demo catalogue, personas and orders reserve these key prefixes (the TC* family, mirrored in that layer's costHints.reservedKeyPrefixes). Additions must not use them. An addition writing rows of its own into a base-owned table uses its own PACK-<NAME>- prefix instead (nvarcharPkPrefix).
idRules.noPerItemTypeNumericTableNote: The contract is prefix-based, not per-itemType-numeric. There is deliberately NO per-itemType numeric range table - do not invent one.

guaranteedRows.permissionGroupsNote: DW 10.26.9 has no AccessUserGroup table - groups ARE AccessUser rows of type 2.
guaranteedRows.usersNote: users and memberships are NOT base rows. They ship in the sample-data layer as merge-mode SqlTable YAML (merge/_sql/AccessUser, merge/_sql/AccessUserGroupRelation) and every entry carries presentOnlyWhen: sampleData - they exist only when an edition activates sampleData: true. An edition with sampleData: false has no AccessUser 100101 / 100102 / 100103 and no memberships, so a sign-in, persona or customer-number binding against them finds no row. All three personas belong to the one B2B account (AccessUser 100100, customer number TC-100200) and carry that same customer number, because contract prices, account-wide favourites and the CSR account listing compare the string exactly. No password is in the data: the sample-data predicate excludes AccessUserPassword and the credential is set online through the Management API UserSetPassword command. A layer probe that needs a persona names it in its requiresFixtures. Only permissionGroups are base-owned (baseOwnedTables.replaceFiltered FILTER-01).

referenceCategory.note: Hidden template category (CategoryType 2) that Dynamicweb's completeness-rule and category-field admin UI reads; required by DemoVerifier Check 2. SHIPPED BY THE BASE since 3.6.0 as two filtered Replace predicates (baseOwnedTables.replaceFiltered FILTER-02 / FILTER-03). Before 3.6.0 the row was claimed here but never shipped: only the Foundry gate synthesised it pre-host-start (Invoke-SeedVerify.ps1 Step 3b), so a consumer deserializing the Distribution outside the gate never received it (Foundry #1304). The gate seed stays and is IF NOT EXISTS-guarded on the category id, so a host it already seeded with a LANG1 translation keeps that row; the base ships the ENU translation, matching every other ENU-keyed display name in the Distribution. Seeded pre-host-start matters because DW caches categories at startup.

contractPrice.note: Ships in the sample-data layer next to the product it scopes to (merge/_sql/EcomPrices/TC-PRICE-CTR-0046.yml); present only when an edition activates sampleData: true. It is the subject of feature-pricing's cart-price contract probe: signed in as the buyer the cart charges 36.90 against a 45.00 list and a 39.60 customer-group row, with zero custom code.

sampleData.note: What the ONE sample-data layer guarantees to an addition that binds to it. Since sample-data 4.0.0 there is exactly one layer of kind sample-data and it carries the whole demo dataset: the browsable Truvio Commerce catalogue, the three personas on one B2B account, twelve orders, the storefront copy, the demo clock and the email-marketing statistics backfill. An addition NEVER binds to the layer directly - it binds to the subjects named here and declares them in its behaviorProbes requiresFixtures. Every subject is absent when an edition sets sampleData false, and a probe that names one is then recorded as a loud SKIP, never a silent pass.

buyer.note: feature-rma's authenticated my-returns probe signs in as this persona, and so does every cart-price and checkout-recurring probe.

csr.note: The CSR customer-center surfaces surface-swift ships resolve against this persona; no probe addresses it by id.

accountAdmin.note: The account surfaces under Customer center/Account resolve against this persona; no probe addresses it by id.

skuValidationProduct.note: feature-reordering's sku-validation probe types this ProductNumber into the Quick Order pad's validation feed.

quantityTierProduct.note: feature-pricing's cart-price tier probe adds quantity 10 and expects 96. Quantity 10 is the only rung the customer-group row TC-PRICE-GRP-0020 (108 at quantity 1, group 1325) cannot also produce, so the observed amount proves the tier ladder rather than price resolution in general.

contractPriceProduct.note: feature-pricing's cart-price contract probe adds quantity 1 signed in as the buyer and expects 36.90.

bomKitProduct.note: feature-bom-configurator's bom-cart-lines probe posts the two slot ids with a NON-default child in each (TCPROD0003, TCPROD0052) and expects two child lines. TCPROD0041 is the fixed Bundle Kit and carries no EcomProductItems slot, so the configurable kit TCPROD0042 is the subject.

subscriptionProduct.note: feature-subscription-orders' checkout-recurring probe buys this plan on PAY2 / SHIP9 and asserts a new EcomRecurringOrder row for the buyer.

deliveredOrder.note: feature-rma's authenticated my-returns probe returns against this completed order; its first line is what the RMA link points at.

rma.note: NOT a sample-data row: feature-rma ships EcomRmas PACK-RMA-0001 and its EcomRmaOrderLines link (id 100301, above the intIdentityFloor) and binds them to the deliveredOrder subject above. Listed here so the whole binding reads from one place.

sampleData.countsNote: EcomProducts 97 = 60 masters + 36 variant rows + the subscription plan TCPROD0061. EcomGroups 16 = 4 top groups + 12 subgroups. An edition that activates sampleData pins these in expectedCounts; a composition that does not activate it carries zero catalogue.

anchors.note: The buyer and CSR anchors name the sample-data rows in guaranteedRows.users: present only when an edition activates sampleData: true. Buyer and CSR share one customer number because they are two contacts on one B2B account. Content anchors (area 3, langPrefix /swift-2) moved to surface-swift (base 3.0.0 ships zero content areas).

repositories.name: ProductsFrontend
repositories.note: ProductsFrontend is the storefront search repository the Swift design package ships (Files/System/Repositories/ProductsFrontend/ at the Swift 2.4.0 tag, alongside ProductsBackend). No layer in this Distribution ships it: it arrives with the host's Swift Files overlay, which is why provisionedByGate is false. Every eCom_ProductCatalog surface this Distribution ships binds it by path - surface-swift Shop PLP (IndexQuery + FacetGroups), surface-swift desktop header search, surface-swift Express Buy, surface-dap-portal Product Assets and Search results, feature-bom-configurator Kit Configurator. A storefront PLP that cannot list products answers HTTP 200 in both of its failure shapes, never a 500. (1) Repository present over an index of zero documents: the page carries an in-page dw-error block with the Lucene 'numHits must be > 0' ArgumentException. (2) Repository absent: the catalog app renders an EMPTY swift-v2_app div with no product list, no facet rail and no error text of any kind, so the page passes a status scan AND an error-text scan while showing nothing. Gate the PLP on a positive subject (at least one product-card element) plus dw-error == 0, never on HTTP status or on the absence of error text alone.

currencyRates.note: EcomCurrencies.CurrencyRate is hundredths against the default currency. The default (EUR, CurrencyIsDefault true on every EUR$$<lang> row) carries 100. A non-default currency at rate 1 renders every price in it a hundred times over, with correct symbol and culture formatting, no error and no log entry (measured on DW 10.28.10: a stored 45.00 served as $4,500.00 at USD rate 1). USD ships at 100: one-to-one parity with the default, a deliberate demo value and not an exchange rate. USD is NOT the currency the Swift storefront serves - surface-swift 1.13.3 binds the Swift area to EUR (AreaEcomCurrencyId). It used to read that way because an UNBOUND area on DW 10.28 resolves the request culture's currency, so an /en-us/ storefront served USD carts and no EUR EcomPrices row matched (Foundry #1232, measured on foundry-sd4v.mydwsite4.com: cart CART783 OrderCurrencyCode USD, TCPROD0046 served 45.00 instead of the contract price 36.90). CurrencyRate reasons about display; EcomPrices.PriceCurrency filtering is what the area binding decides, and every EcomPrices row the Distribution ships is EUR. No shipped row carries a rate at or below 1. The other non-default rows carry the values of the source solution and are not maintained exchange rates; a solution that needs real conversion sets real rates, keeping the default at 100 and every other rate relative to it.

replaceFiltered.note: FILTER-01: only the three permission groups are base-owned on AccessUser; the sample-data account and personas (100100-100103) ship in that layer as merge rows, never serialized into the base.

FILTER-02: only the hidden reference_category template row (CategoryType 2) is base-owned on EcomProductCategory. The concrete tc_* product categories are sample-data merge rows, so this predicate is filtered and never whole-table - a whole-table Replace here would wipe the layer's categories on every re-deserialize (Foundry #1304).
FILTER-03: the ENU display name 'Reference category' that belongs to the FILTER-02 row, on the same filtered reasoning. The tc_*$$ENU translations stay sample-data-owned (Foundry #1304).

baseOwnedTables.note: Additions touching a base-owned table follow idRules (prefix / floor) and must pass the static intersection checks below. Base ships zero catalog (see idRules.baseCatalog) and zero content areas (base split 3.0.0). UrlPath is surface-swift-owned (its single row is a friendly-URL redirect bound to area 3 + a Swift page id - no route targets exist in a framework-only base).

stockLocations.note: Neutral, brand-free stock locations shipped as a whole-table Replace. The baseline DB carried the Swift demo's own 'BikeShop Copenhagen' / 'BikeShop Aarhus' rows, so every composed edition delivered a bike shop's warehouse names; 3.6.0 corrects the names in the base instead of per-edition (Foundry #1303). The IDS 1-3 ARE DELIBERATELY KEPT: all 61 EcomStockUnit rows in the sample-data layer carry StockUnitStockLocationId 3, and EcomShops.ShopStockLocationID (SHOP1 ships 0, meaning 'no single location') addresses the same id space, so a rekey above the intIdentityFloor would orphan the stock units and silently change what a shop points at. These three ids are therefore the one further documented exception to idRules.intIdentityFloor, alongside the permission groups: they are base-owned rows the base does not mint but adopts from the platform baseline. An addition that needs its own stock location mints one at or above 100000.

collisionChecks.rule: Intersect an addition's _sql/<Table>/*.yml filenames (= row keys; composite keys join with $$) with the base's filenames for the same table. Non-empty = FAIL.
WR-10: the same table+filename shipped by >1 active addition = FAIL. A single layer shipping the same key in its own replace+merge is NOT a collision.

07-01: an addition's fragment-shipped _content relative paths must be disjoint from base _content paths (union of both mode trees); cross-layer parity; shipped-files-only (referenced base anchors excluded); declared-footprint parity (every Content entry matches a declared fragmentContent {areaId, path}).

WR-04: (itemType, fields.Id) pairs land as PK rows in shared ItemType_<systemName> tables. The same pair by >1 owner = FAIL. Reusing an id NUMBER across DIFFERENT itemType tables is fine (PK surface is per-table).

registrationAsymmetry.rule: Every csLedger entry with registration 'addin-attribute-config-row' MUST have >=1 matching configRows entry.
registrationAsymmetry.note: Cross-field rule enforced at activation (not JSON-Schema-expressible); locked by tests.

movedToSurfaceSwift.note: Moved by the base split (Swift 2.4 roll-forward): perEnvironmentAreaExclusions, protectedItemTypes, content anchors (areas/langPrefix), navDepth obligation, title-integrity rules. See layers/surface-swift/surface.contract-notes.json.
